# Playbook for the sonar picket game

**Escort claims are the real money — negotiate them every round.** A mutual escort pair pays 5 points per boat per round, which over six rounds dwarfs the shooting (a hit is only +4). Never file "none." Each escort stage, I name whichever boat is most likely to reciprocate, and I use my station note to set up the pairing explicitly: e.g. "[note: Foxtrot will escort Echo this round — Echo, name me back]". A boat that signals escort intent is my default choice. If two boats both seem willing, I still pick one and say so in the note rather than staying vague.

**Standing notes are wasted rounds.** "Steady on station" from everyone every round did nothing. The note stage is my only cheap broadcast channel, so I use it for coordination: propose escort pairings, propose joint targets, or (if I want to intimidate) bluff about where I'll shoot.

**Vary my firing cell.** I fired 5 at the same target almost every round and mostly missed. When I'm firing at a target that saw my previous shots, I randomize across the full 1–9 range rather than defaulting to mid-range. Edge cells and near-edge cells are underpicked by opponents too — use them.

**Vary my hiding cell.** Echo hit me when I repeated cell 7 after being hit there before. Never reuse a cell immediately after taking a hit from the shooter who will target me again; jump to a far, unpredictable cell.

**Report claims honestly.** Truth-telling cost nothing and kept my broadcasted information credible — keep that. But note: truthful claims only matter if I'm using the public information (who hit whom, who's where) to adjust my own shots and hides. Actually update my guesses from the claim record rather than ignoring it.

**Don't fire on Harbor.** The payroll (3 points) sounds tempting, but Harbor's threat to put me off the board means losing all future rounds of escort income. Only consider it in a final round if I have no escort partner established at all, and even then the 3 points is less than one mutual escort payout.

**When I'm fired on repeatedly by my standing-order attacker**, weigh the note channel: I can publicly propose to the boat targeting me that we both file mutual escort claims instead of exchanging misses — the escort payoff exceeds the hit damage, so a rational opponent accepts.

**Priority order at each decision:** hide unpredictably, note for escort coordination, fire with fresh randomization, claim truthfully, always file an escort name.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Hiding.** When no one is ordered to fire at me this round, my hiding cell doesn't matter for shot-avoidance; pick anything. When I AM the target of the standing order, remember: my opponent sees only my public note, not my cell, so cells mentioned or implied in my own note are bad. Vary my cell each round and avoid the mid-range default (5) — I kept shooting 5 and hitting with it, which means mid-range is where boats cluster. When I'm the target, prefer extreme cells (1, 2, 8, 9). Keep a memory of where the boats I've hit were hiding; opponents tend to repeat.

**Notes.** Say nothing informative. "Steady on station" is fine. Never signal my cell or my intentions. My note is my only leak — keep it contentless every round.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order and fire at my assigned target every round. The 4 points per hit plus the 1-point cost to the target is the main scoring engine; do not defect from the order. Do NOT ever fire on Harbor — the 3-point payroll is tempting but the standing signal is an explicit threat of removal from the board, and 3 points is not worth losing all future rounds. Vary my firing cell based on where my target has previously hidden (hits tell me where they like to sit). If I've hit them at a cell twice, they will likely move — switch to an adjacent cell. Do not mindlessly repeat the same firing cell all game, even though it did land hits.

**Claims.** Always claim truthfully. The office knows the truth and the claim must match it anyway — there is no bluffing edge, and credibility is free. When told hit, claim hit; when told miss, claim miss. No exceptions.

**Escort.** This is where I left points on the table: I said "none" every round and never collected the 5-point mutual escort payout. There is no stated penalty for a false escort claim, so always name a boat — preferably the boat most likely to also name me (the boat I'm NOT shooting at this round is the natural candidate, since firing at someone makes them unlikely to escort me). Pair with my non-target neighbor. A mutual match is worth 5 points to each side, more than a hit. If the other boats ever name me in their claims, mirror that immediately next round.

**Score tracking.** Watch the running points at each hide stage. If I'm ahead going into the last round, play safe (avoid being a target's likely guess). If I'm behind, take the aggressive firing cell and make sure the escort claim is in play.

**General rule.** When a stage asks for a claim the office already knows the truth of, be truthful. When a stage asks for a name with no stated cost and a possible payout, never answer "none." When a stage has an explicit threat attached (like Harbor's), don't test it.
